title: The impact of temporal resampling on the safety of clinical reinforcement learning: A simulated trial
abstract: arXiv:2602.06603v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a type of artificial intelligence for making optimal choices. In healthcare, researchers generally use offline RL (ORL), where models are trained and evaluated from retrospective observational data. To accommodate naturally irregular clinical records, researchers often resample the data into uniform time intervals before training (known as binning). However, binning may create counterfactual trajectories that do not represent clinical practice. We first quantified these distortions in patients receiving continuous insulin infusions in the MIMIC-IV intensive care database. Binning reversed the apparent causal order for over 70% of paired glucose measurements and insulin adjustments within the same interval, and frequently masked significant dysglycaemic events and merged distinct treatment decisions together. translated_title: 时间重采样对临床强化学习安全性的影响：一项模拟试验
translated_abstract: 强化学习（RL）是一种用于做出最优决策的人工智能技术。在医疗保健领域，研究人员通常使用离线强化学习（ORL），即基于回顾性观察数据进行模型的训练与评估。为适应临床上天然不规则的数据记录，研究人员通常在训练前将数据重采样为均匀的时间间隔（称为“分箱”）。然而，分箱可能会产生无法代表真实临床实践的反事实轨迹。我们首先在MIMIC-IV重症监护数据库中接受持续胰岛素输注的患者身上量化了这些失真：在同一时间间隔内，超过70%的配对血糖测量与胰岛素调整之间的表观因果顺序被颠倒，且分箱频繁掩盖显著的血糖异常事件，并将不同的治疗决策合并在一起。随后，我们使用30名1型糖尿病虚拟患者开展了一项计算机模拟临床试验……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究通过模拟试验首次量化了时间分箱重采样对临床离线强化学习数据造成的失真，发现其会颠倒血糖与胰岛素之间的因果顺序（超过70%的配对样本）、掩盖血糖异常事件，从而威胁临床强化学习的安全性。
en_tdlr: Through an in silico trial, this study quantifies how temporal binning distorts clinical data for offline reinforcement learning—reversing the causal order of paired glucose-insulin observations in over 70% of cases and masking dysglycaemic events—thereby compromising the safety of clinical RL.
